A JSON Schema of every layered setting (agent, polling, server, workspace), with labels, descriptions, enums, minimums and defaults, is generated from a config registry (`internal/config/settings_fields.go`), printed by `itervox config schema` and published at `https://itervox.dev/schema/settings.schema.json` (`make settings-schema`); tests fail when the loader reads a layered key with no schema entry, when an entry is not read, when a default drifts and when the published file is stale. Settings files may name it in `"$schema"`. A new project-local layer, `.itervox/settings.local.jsonc` (gitignored by `itervox init`/`init --update`), sits between the project file and `WORKFLOW.md`; `itervox config set|unset --local` edits it. The dashboard's Settings page gains an **All settings** section rendered from the schema (served at `GET /api/v1/settings/schema`): generic controls per type, a filter, a tab per layer (User, Project, Project local) naming where every save goes, and a JSON view of the layer's file checked as you type. Saves (`PUT /api/v1/settings/layers/{layer}`, with `GET /api/v1/settings/layers`) go through the one comment-preserving JSONC writer, refuse a stale or invalid save, move the saved keys out of `WORKFLOW.md` for a project or local save, apply settings that have a runtime setter at once through their existing cfgMu setters and report the rest as needing a restart, and refresh the snapshot. The remaining per-field WORKFLOW.md patchers (`tracker.failed_state`, the tracker state lists, `dependencies.analysis_mode`) are replaced by one generic front-matter key writer, `workflow.SetFrontMatterKeys`. `itervox import WORKFLOW.md` converts a Symphony or Itervox v0.x workflow: layered settings to `.itervox/settings.jsonc`, profile prompts to prompt files, Symphony's `codex.*` timeouts and command to `agent.*`, a `WORKFLOW.md.bak`, and a list of every key it could not map. `itervox export --symphony` writes a Symphony `WORKFLOW.md` with the core keys the project sets and the worker prompt, never a literal API key, and lists the Itervox-only features it dropped; an import followed by an export gives back a Symphony workflow's core keys and prompt (`TestImportExportSymphonyRoundTrip`).

- **Rules: layered JSONC rules in every run, with a Rules editor** (#157). Rules are short instructions ("always use pnpm") written once in `~/.itervox/rules.json` (user, never committed; `ITERVOX_USER_RULES` names another file, `off` disables it), `.itervox/rules.json` (project, committed) or `.itervox/rules.local.json` (project local, gitignored). Each rule has an `id`, a `severity` (`must` or `should`), its `text`, an optional `description` and an optional `scope` (projects, profiles, backends; globs allowed). At every dispatch the daemon reads the files again (edits apply to the next run, no restart), merges them (a later layer replaces a rule with the same id, except a user `must` rule, which stands; the conflict is reported in the run's log, the daemon log and the editor), drops the rules out of scope for the run's project, profile and backend, and renders the rest as a `## Rules` block, must rules first, ahead of the profile's SOUL.md and INSTRUCTIONS.md, for workers, reviewers, automation runs and the dependency analyzer. A template that prints `{{ rules }}` or `{{ rules.must }}` (also `rules.should`, `rules.ids`, `rules.hash`) places the rules itself and gets no automatic block. Each run records the rule set it used (`rulesHash` and `ruleIds` on its running row and in run history). The dashboard's new **Rules** page has a tab per layer with a form view (saves rewrite only what changed, through the comment-preserving JSONC writer from #129), a JSON view checked against the schema as you type, and a preview of the effective rules for a profile and an issue; endpoints `GET /api/v1/rules`, `PUT /api/v1/rules/{layer}` (refuses a stale or invalid save) and `GET /api/v1/rules/preview`. The JSON Schema is published at `https://itervox.dev/schema/rules.schema.json`. `itervox init` and `init --update` keep `.itervox/rules.json` committable and gitignore `.itervox/rules.local.json`.
- **Starter templates for `itervox init --template`** (#121). The five templates now write different workflows; the value used to be checked and then ignored. `minimal`: one implementer profile, no reviewer and no automations. `full`: implementer, reviewer, input-responder and deps-analyzer, an auto-review chain (`reviewer_profiles`, `review_quorum: any_block`, `auto_review: true`), and `input_required` and `run_failed` automations. `rate-limit-fallback`: an implementer on each backend, `agent.backend_fallback` mapping the implementer (and runs without a profile) to the other backend, and a `rate_limited` automation that switches to it. `pr-review`: a run reviewer on auto-review and a read-only `pr-reviewer` run by `pr_opened` and by a tracker comment starting with `/review`. `daily-qa`: a read-only `qa` profile run by a daily `cron` automation over issues in the completion state. Each template is schema 2 (`itervox_schema_version: 2`) with every profile's `SOUL.md` and `INSTRUCTIONS.md` under `.itervox/agents/<name>/`, works with every tracker kind (`linear`, `github`, `local`) and both runners, and combines with `--preset cross-review` (the preset adds `reviewer` when a template has none). Without `--template`, init writes the same standard scaffold as before (the flag's default was `minimal`, which wrote that scaffold; it is now empty). `itervox init --help` and the [CLI reference](site/src/content/docs/cli.mdx#starter-templates) describe each template in one line.

- **Backend-aware skills and agents in the dashboard** (#123). A profile's SOUL and INSTRUCTIONS editors now suggest only what the profile's backend can use: a Claude profile gets Claude and shared skills and the subagents, a Codex profile gets Codex and shared skills and Codex custom prompts, and no subagents. The backend is the one the daemon resolves for the draft's command and backend, the same way doctor does. Unknown references are underlined as you type, with doctor's message on hover (F8 / Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+M from the keyboard): the editor sends the text to the new `POST /api/v1/skills/check-refs`, which runs the #86 validator, so the editor and `itervox doctor` report the same references (`MISSING_SKILL_REF`, `MISSING_SUBAGENT_REF`, and with SSH hosts the `USER_SCOPE_REF_ON_SSH` note). The inventory now also lists Codex custom prompts (`~/.codex/prompts/*.md`, new `Prompts` field). The profile form gains a **Skills and agents for Claude** (or **for Codex**) picker that inserts a checked reference, and the issue's **Agent Profile** picker names each profile's backend (from the new `GET /api/v1/skills/profile-backends`) and lists what that backend, or the issue's backend pin, can use. The issue profile picker moved out of `IssueDetailSlide` into `IssueProfilePicker`. New dependency: `@codemirror/lint` (in the lazily loaded editor chunk).
- **PR-event triggers for managed pull requests** (#173). Four automation triggers fire on GitHub activity on a pull request an Itervox run recorded (the run's exit carried the PR URL its worker detected): `pr_check_completed` (a check run or commit status on the head SHA completed; filters `check_names`, `conclusions`), `pr_synchronized` (a new push, including pushes by later runs on the same PR; `pr_opened` still fires once per PR), `pr_review_submitted` (a human or bot review such as Greptile's; filters `review_authors`, `review_states`) and `pr_mergeable_changed` (`mergeable_state` moved, by default into or out of `dirty`; filter `mergeable_states`). New prompt variables: `trigger.pr_number`, `trigger.head_sha`, `trigger.check_name`, `trigger.check_conclusion`, `trigger.mergeable_state`, `trigger.previous_mergeable_state`, `trigger.review_author`, `trigger.review_state`, `trigger.review_id`, `trigger.event_source`. Sources: a poll of the open managed PRs on `polling.automation_interval_ms` with conditional requests (a `304` costs no rate limit; it reads only what a configured rule needs and nothing while no PR-event rule exists; it stretches while GitHub's request budget is low), or, with the new `pr_events.webhook_secret`, signed GitHub `check_run`, `status`, `pull_request` and `pull_request_review` deliveries on `POST /api/v1/webhooks/pr-events` (the poll then reads only each PR's head and `mergeable_state`). The GitHub token is `tracker.api_key` on a GitHub tracker, else `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`, else the `gh` CLI login, so a Linear-tracked project with PRs on GitHub works. A PR no Itervox run recorded never dispatches, and checks or reviews from before the recording run started are ignored. All dispatch goes through the event loop, which dedups per `(PR, head SHA, check, conclusion)`, `(PR, head SHA)`, review ID and `(PR, head SHA, mergeable transition)`; the managed PRs and that ledger persist in `pr_events.json` in the daemon log directory and are dropped when the issue reaches a terminal state. A run a `pr_synchronized` rule dispatched does not fire that rule with its own push. The dashboard's automation editor offers the new triggers and filters and a "PR fix loop" instruction template. Guide: [PR events on managed pull requests](site/src/content/docs/guides/automations.mdx#pr-events-on-managed-pull-requests), with the Greptile fix loop as the worked example.
- **Terminal commands that replace the TUI: `itervox watch`, `logs -f`, quick actions and `--headless`** (#120). `itervox watch` is a read-only, plain-text view of a running daemon (issues waiting for a slot, running, retrying, waiting-for-input, queued automation runs and paused issues) that works over SSH and without a terminal: it redraws on a terminal and otherwise prints only when something other than the ticking run times and token counts changes. `itervox logs [-f] <issue>` prints, and follows, an issue's run log, finding the daemon again (address and token) when it restarts on another port. `itervox pause|resume|dispatch <issue>`, `itervox workers <n>` and `itervox reply <issue> <text>` act through the API and report the result or the daemon's reason for refusing (`reply` says the reply is queued: the daemon applies it only to an issue waiting for input). They find the daemon from `.itervox/dashboard_url` and its token from `ITERVOX_API_TOKEN`, `.itervox/.env` or `<logs-dir>/api-token`. `itervox --headless` starts no terminal UI even on a terminal, logs to stderr and never prints the tokenised dashboard URL; the token-withheld hint now names `--headless` and survives the log redactor. The terminal UI stays the default and now shows a notice pointing to `itervox watch` and `--headless`.

- **Incremental tracker pulls** (#114). Between full pulls, the tracker store asks Linear and GitHub only for the issues updated since its last pull: one paginated request for the whole project (Linear: an `updatedAt` filter including archived and trashed issues; GitHub: `issues?state=all&since=`), instead of re-listing every state set. Changed issues are placed by state, so an edit shows on the board and an issue closed or moved out of the active states leaves the candidates; a trashed, archived or (GitHub) no-longer-labelled issue leaves the store, and a recorded blocker state follows its blocker. A blocker changed locally while a pull was in flight keeps its newer state, and the issues it blocks record that state, not the pull's stale one. A quiet pull changes nothing and does not rewrite the store file. The cursor is the newest update time the tracker itself reported (no clock agreement needed), saved in `tracker_store.json`, and each pull asks from one minute before it; GitHub lists newest first, so an issue edited while the pages are read is listed twice or on the next pull, never skipped. A GitHub issue closed without `closed` among the terminal states leaves the store (a full pull would not list it either). A full pull that lists an issue twice, because it changed between two requests, keeps the newer copy. A failed pull keeps the cursor and retries after 5 s, doubling up to `sync_interval_ms`. A full pull still runs every `tracker.store.full_sync_interval_ms` (default 1 hour), to catch moves to another project or repository and deleted GitHub issues, and a pull a webhook asks for (#131: an issue the store does not hold, or a flooded delivery queue) is always a full one; until then the state an issue records for a blocker outside the project can be up to that old. Measured with `go test -tags measure -run TestMeasureTrackerRequests ./cmd/itervox/` (the real daemon against a counting fake GitHub API, an idle 40-issue project with two active labels, every interval scaled down 30×, so one run is one simulated hour): with the dashboard open, 4,558 → 71 tracker requests per hour (−98.4%); the daemon alone, 238 → 71 (−70.2%) at the default 1-minute sync, 238 → 41 (−82.8%) at a 2-minute sync, and 238 → 6 (−97.5%) at a 10-minute sync (the webhook safety-net interval). The baseline is this build with the store off (the v0.2.2 polling path), counted at the fake server. Reads by ID (the per-tick state check of each running issue, the claim check) are not reduced and are not in this idle scenario.

- **Claim check before every agent start** (#116). With the tracker store on, list reads come from a local copy that can be up to one sync behind. Now, just before any agent starts (a dispatch, retry, reviewer, automation run, answered question or backend-fallback re-dispatch), Itervox reads the issue once more from the tracker by ID and starts it only if it is still eligible there: an issue a person closed, moved out of an active state or deleted since the last pull is not started, and the store's copy is corrected by that read. An issue the tracker no longer has also leaves the store's local copy at once. When a person changes an issue after Itervox queued a state write for it, and the write is still queued when the issue is next about to start, the person's change wins: the queued write is dropped, with a warning in the log and a status-history row (`pending_write_dropped`); a state difference found by the check is recorded too (`claim_check`). A write the outbox already delivered before that is not undone (the outbox delivers within seconds and does not read before writing). The tick's dispatch reuses the issue read it already made before dispatching, and retries, answered questions and resumed pending reviews reuse theirs; reviewers, automation runs and the backend-fallback re-dispatch make one read by ID each. When the tracker cannot be read, nothing is lost: the tick dispatches the issue on a later tick, an automation waits in the automation queue (`tracker_unavailable`), and a reviewer gets a retry. A reviewer's retry is now admitted in a non-active `completion_state` too (it used to be dropped there). A reviewer chain whose next reviewer is refused is closed instead of waiting forever.

- **Release acceptance checks** (#137). A manual `Release acceptance` workflow (environment `acceptance`, required reviewers recommended) runs two checks that need real accounts. **self-hosted**: Itervox built from the dispatched ref completes a test issue of this repository with a real Claude agent and opens a pull request; only that issue is touched (the run uses its own per-run `smoke-<issue>-<run>:*` state labels), and the daemon log and agent sessions are uploaded as the record. **deploy-gcp** (billable): the deploy kit provisions a GCP VM, bootstraps the release under test, passes `itervox doctor --deploy`, serves the dashboard through the IAP tunnel, and tears down what it created, pass or fail. Both are scripts in `deploy/acceptance/` that also run locally (`--dry-run` / `--keep`), covered by stub tests in `make deploy-test`. Runbook: [docs/release-checks.md](docs/release-checks.md). The deploy check refuses an instance or data-disk name that already exists and its teardown deletes only what the run created; the self-hosted run's active labels are unique per issue and run (and deleted at exit), so an issue a failed earlier run left labelled is never dispatched; and the self-hosted script, with its stub test, runs without `setsid` (macOS).

- **Upgrade test from v0.2.1** (#138). `TestUpgradeFromV021` starts from a project exactly as v0.2.1 left it (its `itervox init` output, and ledgers written by v0.2.1's own code: paused issues with a reason, an open backend breaker, a pending review, an unanswered question, run history and an undelivered outbox state move and comment), runs this build's `itervox init --update` (which leaves the workflow as it is and adds the `!.itervox/issues/` carve-out to the root `.gitignore`), starts the real daemon against a local fake GitHub API, and checks that every ledger is read back intact. It runs in CI with the rest of the Go tests. See [docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md#upgrade-test-release-check).

- **Per-issue budgets and a cost report** (#136). `agent.budget.tokens` and `agent.budget.cost_usd` cap what one issue may use across all its runs (implementer, retries, reviewers and automation runs). When an issue reaches either, its agent is stopped and it is paused with the new pause reason `budget_exceeded` (in `pauseReasons`; the dashboard notifies). Retries, automations and an answered question pause it again instead of starting it while it is over budget; raise the budget and resume to continue. The totals are kept in `issue_spend.json` in the logs directory, so a restart does not reset them. `itervox report costs [--days N] [--json]` prints tokens and estimated cost per issue and per day. Cost is estimated from Claude runs; Codex reports none. A run's final tokens and cost are settled at its exit, failed or not, counted once against what its progress updates already reported, and a failed run that has used the budget is paused rather than retried.

- **Reviewer verdicts in the dashboard** (#135). Issue detail shows the issue's latest review: each reviewer's verdict, reasons and line comments, and the quorum result once every reviewer has run ("Reviewing…" while a chain is in progress), from a new `review` field on `GET /api/v1/issues/{identifier}`. A single-reviewer setup now records its verdict too. **Re-run review** in the panel (like the existing **Review** button and `POST /api/v1/issues/{identifier}/ai-review`) now starts a fresh review by the whole configured chain from its first reviewer, with the previous verdicts cleared; it used to run only `reviewer_profile` and, with several reviewers configured, recorded nothing. A finished review now stays in issue detail after the issue completes, for as long as the issue's status history is kept (7 days after it was last seen changing); before, the next poll could drop it, taking the reasons and the **Re-run review** control with it.

- **Local tracker: edits are picked up at once** (#133). The daemon watches `.itervox/issues/` (fsnotify) and polls immediately when an issue file is added, edited or removed outside Itervox, so an issue moved to an active state is dispatched right away instead of at the next `polling.interval_ms`. While the directory is watched, reads are served from the watched copy instead of rescanning the directory on every call. A rescan every 10 seconds covers missed events, filesystems without change events, and a directory that is removed or recreated (which is watched again); Itervox's own writes do not trigger a poll. New dependency: `github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify` v1.10.1. A watched directory that cannot be read (replaced by a file, say) is reported by every read and by `itervox doctor`, as without a watch; the cached issues are not served as current until a scan succeeds again.

- **Tracker webhooks for Linear and GitHub** (#131). With `tracker.webhooks.enabled` (and the tracker store on), Itervox receives issue webhooks on `POST /api/v1/webhooks/linear` or `/github` and re-reads each changed issue by ID, so a change made in the tracker reaches the board within seconds with no list request; the store's full pull slows to `tracker.webhooks.safety_net_interval_ms` (default 10 minutes) to repair missed deliveries. Every delivery must carry an HMAC-SHA256 signature made with `tracker.webhooks.secret`; unsigned, wrongly signed and (Linear) more-than-a-minute-old deliveries are dropped with `401`. Each named issue is read back by ID and checked against the scope (the project filter on Linear, the repository on GitHub): an in-scope issue is placed, a new one included; one that left the project, or was deleted or transferred, leaves the store; another project's issue costs that one read. The secret must be at least 16 characters. The route needs no bearer token and passes the unauthenticated-mode Host guard, since the signature authenticates it. New metrics: `itervox_tracker_webhooks_total{tracker,result}` and `itervox_tracker_store_pulls_total{trigger}`. Guide: [Tracker webhooks](site/src/content/docs/guides/tracker-webhooks.mdx), covering direct delivery, `gh webhook forward` and a tunnel relay. A by-ID read never undoes a local change made while it was in flight (a state write through the store, a removal), and a removal for an issue the store does not hold yet still stops a pull in flight from adding it. On GitHub, an issue is in scope only when the answer names the repository and the number asked for, so an issue transferred to the same number in another repository is left out.

- **Settings files: user and project defaults in JSONC** (#129). `agent`, `polling`, `workspace` and `server` settings can now also come from `~/.itervox/settings.jsonc` (every project; `ITERVOX_USER_SETTINGS` names another file, `off` disables it) and `.itervox/settings.jsonc` (this project), under `WORKFLOW.md`: defaults < user < project < workflow, maps merged key by key. `itervox config show` prints each effective value and the layer it came from (`--json` too; secrets hidden). `itervox config set KEY VALUE [--user]` and `itervox config unset KEY` edit a settings file and keep its comments; a wrong-typed value or a change the workflow will not load with is refused, and `set` warns when a higher layer overrides the key or Itervox does not read it. A settings file that sets another section (the tracker stays in `WORKFLOW.md`) or does not parse stops the load with an error. A running daemon applies a change when it next loads `WORKFLOW.md`. `go test` never reads the developer's own user file. New dependency: `github.com/tailscale/hujson` (JSONC parsing and comment-preserving edits). `server.allow_unauthenticated` and its deprecated spelling `allow_unauthenticated_lan` count as one setting across layers, so a higher layer's value under either spelling wins and a user file cannot turn off authentication a project's WORKFLOW.md requires. Dashboard and TUI saves of these sections (workers, retries, switch budget, dispatch strategy, inline input, reviewer, SSH hosts, workspace auto-clear) now write `.itervox/settings.jsonc`, keeping its comments, and move the key (and its deprecated spelling) out of `WORKFLOW.md` in the same save, restoring the settings file if the `WORKFLOW.md` step fails.

- **`make chaos` and a nightly chaos CI job** (#126). The orchestrator and tracker tests run over and over (`-race -count -cpu 1,2,4`) while busy loops saturate every CPU, which is how the ordering races fixed in v0.2.2 were reproduced. Every night on the default branch, on demand, and on a pull request labelled `ci:chaos`; a failing package uploads its verbose log, where a hung test's timeout panic carries every goroutine's stack. The tests get a throwaway git config, so a developer's commit signing is never asked to sign their commits. Settings: `CHAOS_COUNT`, `CHAOS_RUN`, `CHAOS_PACKAGES`, `CHAOS_CPU`, `CHAOS_HOGS`, `CHAOS_TIMEOUT`, `CHAOS_OUT`.

- **Local tracker store** (#113). With `tracker.store.enabled: true`, Itervox keeps the tracked Linear or GitHub issues in `.itervox/tracker_store.json` and serves the orchestrator's and dashboard's list reads from it; ticks no longer call the tracker's list endpoints, and the board keeps working through a tracker outage. A background sync re-pulls every `tracker.store.sync_interval_ms` (default 60s). A restart serves from the file; a cold start pulls exactly once. On by default since #132.

- **Deploy skill and `itervox secret`** (#88). `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` walks an agent through deploying to AWS, GCP or Azure with the shipped kit: it asks for cloud, region, size and access method, provisions with `provision.sh` or the OpenTofu modules (confirming before anything billable), bootstraps the VM, sets secrets, runs `itervox doctor --deploy`, starts the service and prints the tunnel command and dashboard URL. `itervox secret set KEY` writes a value to `.itervox/.env` without it ever appearing on a command line or in output (hidden prompt or stdin; written in a form the daemon's loader reads back exactly, or refused; atomic, `0600`, keeps a symlink and the file's owner; `--replace` to rotate), and `itervox secret list` shows which values are set without printing them. The deploy README's bootstrap example now pins the current release, and a test keeps the deploy docs' `--version` examples on the newest release in this changelog.

- **Autocomplete in the profile prompt editor** (#87). Typing `/` or `@` in the SOUL, INSTRUCTIONS or automation instruction editor lists matching skills and subagents from the skills inventory (with description and source: project, user or plugin); `{{` lists the Liquid variables profile prompts get (`issue.*`, `attempt`, `run.*`, plus `trigger.*` for automations); `|` inside `{{ … }}` lists common filters. Arrow keys, Enter and Escape work (Tab still moves focus; a caret moved away closes the list; Enter during IME composition is left to the IME), the textarea keeps its textbox role with `aria-autocomplete`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant`, and the suggestion count is announced. See [Agent Profiles](site/src/content/docs/guides/agent-profiles.mdx#autocomplete-in-the-prompt-editor).

- **Local tracker: `tracker.kind: local`** (#85). Issues are Markdown files in `.itervox/issues/` (`ITX-12.md`): front matter for title, state, priority, labels, `blocked_by` and branch, the body as the description, and comments under `## Comments`. No account, API key or labels. Edits made by hand are picked up on the next poll without a restart; the dashboard, Itervox and agent actions (create issue, comment, move state) write the files atomically, and everything survives a restart. A file that does not parse is logged and listed by `itervox doctor`, its last good version keeps being served, and Itervox does not write to it until it is fixed. `itervox init --tracker local` writes the workflow and an example issue; `itervox quickstart` chooses it when there is no `LINEAR_API_KEY` and no github.com remote (it used to stop there); `itervox demo --tracker local` runs the demo over issue files. The issues are committable: `init` adds `!.itervox/issues/` to a root `.gitignore` that hides `.itervox/`. `project_slug` is the optional identifier prefix (default `ITX`). See the [Local issues guide](site/src/content/docs/guides/local-issues.mdx).

- **`/itervox` comment commands on GitHub issues** (#84). With `tracker.comment_commands.enabled: true`, a maintainer's comment starting with `/itervox run [profile]`, `/itervox stop` or `/itervox review` dispatches the issue (resuming it or moving it to the first active state, optionally under a profile), stops its agent, or dispatches the reviewer, acknowledged with a 👍 reaction (😕 and a short reply when it cannot). Only users with write access (or in `allow`) are obeyed; bots, Itervox's own comments and the token's own account (which agents use; opt in with `allow_token_user`) never are; others are ignored, or answered with `reply_to_unauthorized`. Each comment is acted on once: its ID is recorded in `.itervox/comment_commands.json` before acting, so retries and restarts never repeat it. One repository-wide comment request per 30 seconds; permission checks are cached for 10 minutes. Documented in the GitHub guide with the security model.
- **"Claude writes, Codex reviews": the cross-review preset and read-only reviewers** (#79). `itervox init --preset cross-review` (offered `[y/N]` in a terminal when both `claude` and `codex` are installed) adds a reviewer on the other backend next to `reviewer`, with `reviewer_profiles: [reviewer-<other>, reviewer]`, `review_quorum: any_block` and `auto_review: true`, so every successful run is reviewed on both backends; `--runner codex` gives the reverse. Every reviewer is now **read-only**: the default reviewer prompt, `init`'s `reviewer_prompt` and the reviewer `SOUL.md`/`INSTRUCTIONS.md` ask for a verdict instead of a commit and push; Itervox no longer pushes the branch or commits the handoff for a reviewer run; a reviewer that moves `HEAD` (commit, pull, reset), pushes to one of the workspace's remotes (seen with `git ls-remote`, by remote name or URL, with or without a new commit, even after a reset; deleting a remote branch is not detected) or edits files outside Itervox's handoff/review/evidence directories is flagged on the issue and its verdict counts as a block; the starting point is kept across retries of the same review and retaken for each new one; a verdict from an earlier round is removed before a reviewer runs, so it is never reused. Every reviewer, a single one included, records a verdict (`approve`/`block`, `reasons`, and new line `comments`), gets the diff against the base branch plus only the latest handoff, and has its verdict posted on the issue; a closed multi-reviewer quorum posts its result too. Reviewers 2..n of a chain now get `reviewer_prompt` like the first. New guide: Cross-review preset, with the expected cost (each reviewer is a separate run).
- **`itervox doctor --upgrade`: only the upgrade notes that apply** (#82). It reads the workflow's front matter (raw, so a config that no longer loads is still explained), the environment with `.itervox/.env` loaded, the project's runtime files and the machine, and prints each v0.2.1 upgrade note or breaking change that applies with why, the concrete fix and a link to the note: worktrees or runtime state left in the v0.2.0 shared or per-slug locations (5), port 8090 already taken with no port set (6), `dependencies.auto_analyze` (9), the token no longer printed under a systemd unit (10), invalid SSH host-key checking values (11), `.WORKFLOW.md.lock` not gitignored (12), an unauthenticated daemon without `server.allowed_hosts` (13, 14), a pre-v0.2.1 PID file (15), an old systemd unit without `--shutdown-grace` / `KillMode=mixed` (17, 22), `PORT` set (19, judged as the daemon parses it), `ITERVOX_LOG_FORMAT=json` (20), token auth now required on loopback for a project that ran an older daemon there (#48), `server.allow_unauthenticated_lan`, and a backend that contradicts its command, including `agent.command`'s `claude` default and `rate_limited` `switch_to_backend` (CORE-115). With nothing to change it prints one "all clear" line and exits 0; otherwise it exits 1. Documented in the CLI reference, the deployment guide, the runbook and the compatibility notes.
- **Done needs evidence: `agent.profiles.<name>.require_evidence`** (#80). Off by default. With a list such as `[test, lint, ci]`, a successful run of that profile moves its issue to `completion_state` only with proof: each named check as a passing entry (command and output) in `.itervox/evidence/<profile>.json` (`{{ run.evidence_path }}`), stamped with the commit the checks ran on so old evidence never counts for new code (later commits may only touch `.itervox/`, such as the handoff commit, and no tracked file may have an uncommitted change), and `ci` as only-passing checks on the run's pull request (`gh pr checks`). The prompt gets an `## Evidence (required)` block. Without the evidence the issue is not moved: the run ends input-required with a "Needs evidence" reason listing what is missing, and a reply resumes the agent, whose run is checked again. Reviewer and automation runs are not gated. A non-list value (e.g. `require_evidence: true`) is a config error.
- **Agent-ready issue template** (#83). `itervox init` and `itervox quickstart` offer, after confirmation, to add `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/agent-task.md` for a new GitHub workflow (`init --issue-template` / `quickstart --yes` skip the question), and never write over an existing file; `init` asks only in a terminal, so scripted runs are unchanged; on a project that already has a workflow, `init --issue-template` adds only the template. For Linear they offer to print the same sections, with blockers pointing at Linear's own relation. Sections: goal, acceptance criteria, likely files or areas, how to verify, out of scope, and blockers in the phrasing the GitHub adapter parses (`Blocked by #12, #15`; left unfilled it declares none). The template sets no labels, so a new issue is not dispatched before it is filled in. Documented in the GitHub Issues guide.
- **Opt-in "Shipped with Itervox" PR footer and README badge** (#81). `agent.pr_footer: true` (default `false`) appends a one-line `Shipped with [Itervox](https://github.com/vnovick/itervox)` footer to the body of each pull request an agent run opens on its own branch (a PR merely linked from the issue, which may be a person's, is left alone), with `gh pr edit` after a successful worker run. A hidden `<!-- itervox:shipped -->` marker keeps it to once per PR, so later runs on the same PR never duplicate it. The configuration docs include a README badge snippet.
- **`itervox demo`: try Itervox in about a minute with no keys** (#76). It writes a throwaway memory-tracker workflow in a temporary (or `--dir`) directory and runs the normal daemon with a scripted agent (`internal/agent/demoagent`) instead of `claude`/`codex`, so no agent CLI or tracker credentials are needed. The board shows ten `DEMO-n` issues moving through In Progress (with streamed activity and a fake pull request), input required (answered automatically), a failure and retry, In Review and Done within about a minute, and the dashboard header shows a **Demo mode** badge (`demoMode` in the state snapshot). Logs, workspaces and runtime files stay in the scratch directory; the dashboard opens in the browser unless `--no-open`.
- **`itervox quickstart`: one command from a repository to a running board** (#74). It detects the tracker (Linear when `LINEAR_API_KEY` is set, otherwise GitHub from a github.com `origin`) and the agent CLI (`claude`, else `codex`), writes a schema-2 `WORKFLOW.md` and agent profiles like `itervox init` (an existing schema-2 workflow is used as is; an older one is migrated only after confirmation), offers the `gh` CLI's token and saves it to `.itervox/.env` after confirmation, creates missing GitHub state labels after confirmation, runs `itervox doctor` and stops with its report on any error, then starts the daemon in its own session, waits for `/api/v1/ready` and prints the dashboard URL and the API token file. Re-running is safe: it never overwrites without asking and reports a daemon that is already running. Flags: `--yes`, `--no-start`, `--tracker`, `--runner`. The README and getting-started guide now lead with it.
- **Stacked pull requests target their blocker's branch** (#73). With `dependencies.stacked_prs: true`, a run whose worktree is stacked on its blocker's branch now gets `{{ run.pr_base_branch }}` (the blocker's branch; `workspace.base_branch` on other runs) and a `## Stacked Branch` prompt block telling the agent to open the pull request with `--base <blocker-branch>`, and after a successful worker run Itervox points the issue's open pull request (opened by the run or already linked from the issue) at that branch with `gh pr edit --base` unless it already matches. A worktree counts as stacked only when the blocker's branch is in its history and has commits `workspace.base_branch` lacks. When a dependent is restacked onto `base_branch` after its blocker lands (or already sits there), its pull request is retargeted to `base_branch` the same way, off the event loop. `gh` errors (for example a blocker branch not pushed to the remote) are logged, not fatal. An issue whose only unresolved blocker is in `tracker.completion_state` (done and in review, not merged) is now dispatched right away, stacked on that blocker's branch, so a chain of dependent issues no longer waits for each merge. The blocker's branch is the one its run used: Linear's branch name (now fetched with blocker relations), else `itervox/<identifier>`; on GitHub a blocker carrying the `completion_state` label now reads as that state instead of none. If the blocker's branch is not available locally, the fresh worktree is removed before any agent runs (a dependent branch that already has its own commits is kept) and the issue waits for the blocker as before; an existing worktree that is not stacked on the blocker is kept and the issue waits the same way, until the blocker leaves review or changes. Without `stacked_prs`, every non-terminal blocker still holds the dependent.
- **Claude Code subagents in the skills inventory, and checked skill/subagent references in profile prompts** (#86). The inventory now scans `.claude/agents/**/*.md` in the project and user home plus agents declared by plugins (name, description, tools, model, size, source), and the Settings → Skills card lists them in a **Subagents** section. Profile `SOUL.md` / `INSTRUCTIONS.md` references in explicit forms (`@agent-name`, `` `name` skill ``, `` `a`, `b`, and `c` skills ``, `` `name` subagent ``; fenced code blocks ignored, including inside lists and quotes) are resolved for the backend the profile actually runs on, computed with the dispatcher's helpers and checked against its resolver by an exhaustive test; a missing one is reported as `MISSING_SKILL_REF` / `MISSING_SUBAGENT_REF` in the dashboard's issues list and as a `WARNING:` line in `itervox doctor` (exit code unchanged). With SSH hosts configured, references that exist only outside the repository (user home or a user-installed plugin) get a `USER_SCOPE_REF_ON_SSH` note. The skills cache now also notices a new agent file (including the first one, or one added to an empty subfolder) and no longer reports itself stale because an optional file such as `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/agents` does not exist.
- **GitHub tracker setup guide** (#77), on the site (`/guides/github-issues/`) and in `docs/github-tracker.md`: state labels with `gh label create` commands and `itervox doctor --fix`, `p0`–`p3` priority labels and how they order dispatch, blocker phrases in the issue body, `#42` identifiers and the template variables (including which ones are unset until filled and must be guarded under strict variables), `gh auth`, and a GitHub-vs-Linear comparison (no project filter, no sub-issue gating, per-issue state reads). Linked from getting-started, and `itervox doctor` prints the link with every GitHub label problem. The rewrite also corrects three errors in the previous guide: its example prompt used `{{ issue.number }}`, which does not exist and fails every dispatch under strict template variables (use `{{ issue.identifier }}`); `active_states: [open]` matches only issues labelled `open`, not all open issues; and `completion_state: closed` adds a `closed` label rather than closing the issue.
- **`itervox doctor` checks GitHub state labels; `doctor --fix` creates the missing ones** (#75). The GitHub tracker maps every state to an issue label, and a state whose label does not exist matched nothing: no issue was dispatched or moved and nothing reported why. Doctor now lists each configured state label missing on the repository (active, working, completion, terminal except `closed`, backlog and failed states, case-insensitive) with the exact `gh label create` command, and exits `1`. API failures are reported but never fail doctor; Linear workflows skip the check. `itervox doctor --fix` creates the missing labels after a `[y/N]` prompt (the API time limit starts after the answer); `--yes` / `-y` skips it for CI. A repair that fails part-way exits `1` and still lists the labels it did not create.

- **An event feed with a cursor, and pause/resume for all dispatch** (#213). `GET /api/v1/feed?since=<seq>&limit=` returns the notable events after a cursor — `run_started`, `run_finished`, `run_failed`, `input_required`, `input_answered`, `review_verdict`, `pr_opened`, `pr_merged`, `guardrail_blocked`, `guardrail_approved`, `lesson_proposed`, `dispatch_paused`, `dispatch_resumed` — each with a monotonically increasing `seq` (assigned only by the event loop, never reused across restarts), `ts`, `kind`, the issue and a small structured payload (run id, profile, backend, terminal reason, verdict, PR URL, guardrail kind, redacted pause reason) that never holds agent output, prompt text, questions, replies, failure text or guardrail command lines; the response carries `nextSeq`, `headSeq`, `oldestSeq`, `hasMore` and `truncated: true` when the cursor is older than the window. The feed is `State.Feed` / `State.FeedSeq`, bounded to the newest 5000 events and 7 days, persisted to `feed.jsonl` in the daemon log directory through the ledger writer; in-loop handlers that already observe each transition append to it, and the `merge_pr` action's off-loop success path sends `EventFeedRecorded` without blocking. The `/api/v1/events` stream gains `event: feed` with `{"seq":N}` on connect and whenever a delivered snapshot's new `feedSeq` moved, riding the existing 4 Hz coalescing; the snapshot gains `feedSeq`. `POST /api/v1/dispatch/pause` (`{reason?, until?}`) and `POST /api/v1/dispatch/resume` set `State.DispatchPaused` through the event loop: running agents continue, and nothing new starts — tick dispatch, pending-input resumes, automations and pending reviews see no slots, retries stay due without a tracker read or a spent attempt, a backend-fallback re-dispatch is held as a retry, and reviewers are kept as pending reviews (a reviewer chain continues where it stopped) — all re-admitted on resume, which also drains held automations at once. Idle issues show the ineligible reason `dispatch_paused`, and automations queue with that reason. The pause persists to `dispatch_paused.json`, survives restarts and reloads, and ends by itself at its `until` (on the first tick after it). The snapshot shows `dispatchPaused` (`null`, or the reason, until and start) and advertises the `dispatch_pause` capability; `GET /api/v1/summary` reports `paused`, `pauseReason` and `pausedUntil`, all part of its ETag. New CLI forms: `itervox pause [--reason r] [--for 2h]` and `itervox resume` without an issue (with an issue they act on that issue as before), and `itervox watch` shows the pause. The dashboard's status strip has a **Pause dispatch** / **Resume dispatch** toggle with a confirm and a *Dispatch paused* chip; the Mac app's tray has **Pause all agents** / **Resume all agents** for every reachable local daemon and shows *dispatch paused* per project. Guide: [Pause dispatch & event feed](site/src/content/docs/guides/pause-and-feed.mdx); API: [docs/api.md](docs/api.md#event-feed); CLI: [cli](site/src/content/docs/cli.mdx#pause-and-resume-all-dispatch).

### Changed

- **One config format: tracker, hooks, dependencies and automations are layered settings** (#239). `tracker`, `hooks`, `dependencies` and `automations` join `agent`, `hub`, `polling`, `server` and `workspace` as sections of the user (`~/.itervox/settings.jsonc`), project (`.itervox/settings.jsonc`, committed) and local (`.itervox/settings.local.jsonc`, gitignored) settings files, all in the published schema ([`settings.schema.json`](site/public/schema/settings.schema.json): every key with its type, default and description; `automations` is a list section a file sets whole). `WORKFLOW.md` holds the prompt — its body stays the Liquid template and the import/export format — plus the schema marker, the non-layered sections, `agent.profiles`, `agent.available_models` and the legacy `agent.reviewer_prompt`. Precedence is now defaults < user < `WORKFLOW.md` front matter < project < local: the user file holds personal defaults a project's front matter overrides, and the project and local files override the front matter. Front-matter keys still apply; `itervox doctor` names each as deprecated and where it moves, the daemon's startup log does once, and a key also set in the project or local file is reported once as a conflict (the file wins); `itervox config set` notes such a copy. `itervox init` (every template) and `itervox quickstart` write the layered sections to `.itervox/settings.jsonc`, so a new project loads with nothing deprecated. **Migration:** `itervox init --update` moves the layered front-matter keys into `.itervox/settings.jsonc` after the schema-2 steps — `WORKFLOW.md.bak` first, YAML comments carried over as `//` comments and the settings file's own comments kept, a key the file already sets keeping the file's value, and the move refused if the merged config would change; `--dry-run` prints the new file and writes nothing. **Secrets** stay out of settings files: a `$VAR` reference moves as written and is never resolved; a key holding an inline secret (or a URL with a password) stays in `WORKFLOW.md` and is named, never printed; the Settings page and `itervox config set` refuse an inline secret. `itervox import` moves the same sections. **Saves:** the Settings page's All settings section lists the new sections and saves them to the layer its tab picks, applying the tracker state lists, the failed state and `dependencies.analysis_mode` live through their existing `cfgMu` setters (the allowlist and reload behaviour are unchanged); the dedicated tracker-states, failed-state, analysis-mode, project-filter, tracker-scope and tracker-filter saves and the automations editor (including the cascade when a profile is renamed, disabled or deleted, which also keeps `policy.move_to_state` now) write the settings file through the same comment-preserving writer, and `itervox models refresh` writes `agent.available_models` to the settings file that sets it. The per-key WORKFLOW.md writers for these sections (`workflow.SetFrontMatterKeys`, `PatchAutomationsBlock` and the tracker-line editors) are removed. Configuration: [Settings files](site/src/content/docs/configuration.mdx#settings-files-jsonc-layers), [docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md); CLI: [`itervox init --update`](site/src/content/docs/cli.mdx).

- **The Mac app does far less work while idle: adaptive polling, an in-process registry read and `GET /api/v1/summary` with an ETag** (#212). The app refreshes every 3 seconds only while a daemon (local or remote) has an agent running or retrying, a question waiting or resuming, or a start or stop is pending, and every 15 seconds otherwise; pointing at or clicking the menu-bar icon and focusing an app window refresh at once. It reads `~/.itervox/daemons/*.json` itself (new `registry.rs`, the same liveness rule as `itervox status`: live pid, the project's `daemon.pid` naming it, the pid lock held for a lock-marked pid file; stale and unreadable records deleted) instead of spawning `itervox status --all --json` — which ran `pgrep` and was polled every 25 ms — on every refresh; the command still runs at start, on menu open (at most every 30 s) and **Refresh Now**, and whenever a record's `schema_version` is unknown, and daemons it found by process scan are kept while their pid lives. A shared fixture (`cmd/itervox/testdata/daemon_registry_parity.json`) runs in the Go and Rust suites so both produce the same rows. The new `GET /api/v1/summary` (behind the bearer token, built from the state snapshot) returns the version, project name, counts (running, retrying, paused issues, input required, pending input resume, recent failures), a daemon-wide `paused` flag (the #213 dispatch pause) and an `etag`; its `ETag` header covers every field but `generatedAt` plus the identity of each question and failure, and `If-None-Match` gets `304` with no body. Each daemon, local or through a tunnel, is read over one kept-alive connection: the summary with the last ETag, and `/api/v1/state` only after a `200` (or from a daemon without the endpoint). On macOS and BSD, the external-session scan runs `lsof` once per agent process and reuses the result while the process keeps its pid and start time (from `ps` `etime`), for up to 2 minutes. API: [docs/api.md](docs/api.md#get-summary); guide: [Mac app](site/src/content/docs/guides/mac-app.mdx#projects).

- **The dashboard re-renders less and downloads less** (#211). Components no longer subscribe to the whole state snapshot, whose `generatedAt` changes on every frame: the Notifications tab count, the Notifications view, the Review Queue and the Automations activity tab now select only the fields they read (`useShallow`), the issue-cache invalidation hook watches the store with `subscribe` instead of rendering, and the board is memoised with stable props, so it no longer re-renders on frames that only move `generatedAt` or change fields it does not show (automation queue, failures, outbox, capacity, SSH hosts). A guard run by `pnpm lint` (`web/scripts/snapshotSelectorGuard.mjs`) fails on `useItervoxStore((s) => s.snapshot)` (and its variants) outside the store and SSE modules. The Deps tab's graph (`@xyflow/react` and its stylesheet) loads only when the tab opens. The cron builder (antd + `react-js-cron`, a 295 kB chunk) is replaced by a light cron input — presets, one field per cron field, the raw expression and a plain-English preview — that validates with the daemon's parser rules and blocks saving an invalid expression; a shared fixture (`internal/schedule/testdata/cron_parity.json`) runs in both the Go and the dashboard test suites so the two cannot drift. Board columns with more than 100 cards mount only the cards near the viewport; keyboard drag and drop out of and into such a column is covered by tests, pointer and touch drags use the same column drop targets and drag overlay, and the dragged card stays mounted while its column scrolls. Build output, before → after: Dashboard chunk 361 kB → 175 kB (no xyflow), CronWidget chunk 295 kB → gone (the cron input adds 5 kB to the Automations chunk), the Deps graph is a separate 188 kB chunk, all JavaScript 2.12 MB → 1.83 MB; the initial load is unchanged at about 500 kB. A bundle budget (`web/scripts/checkBundleBudget.mjs`, `pnpm bundle:budget`, `make web-bundle-budget`) runs in `make verify` and the Web CI job: it caps total, initial-load and per-chunk JavaScript and fails if xyflow returns to the Dashboard chunk or antd / `react-js-cron` to any chunk.

- **The daemon's dashboard stream costs a fraction of the CPU** (#210). With dashboards open, the daemon rebuilt and re-encoded the full state snapshot once per connected client on every change; now the first `/api/v1/events` client of a change encodes it and every other client writes the same bytes (an immutable cached frame keyed by a broadcast version; a client that connects after a quiet period of over a second gets a fresh one), frames are written with plain writes, and state-change notifications reach the dashboards at most four times a second — the first change after a quiet period at once, later ones folded into one snapshot at the end of the 250 ms window, so the latest state always arrives and an input-required or approval request waits at most 250 ms. On a demo daemon (3 scripted agents, 500 issues, 5 dashboards, 60 s) daemon CPU fell from 4.1% to 1.8%, allocation from 6.9 MB/s to 2.0 MB/s (2.9 to 1.3 GC/s) and stream traffic from 787 KB/s to 200 KB/s; `BenchmarkSSEFanout10Clients` went from 4.1 ms to 0.8 ms per change delivered to ten clients. **Snapshot shape:** `candidateSeen` is no longer serialized (no dashboard, TUI, Mac app or documented consumer read it; the deps auto-analyze scheduler still reads it in process), and `dependencyGraphNodes` lists only issues that are an endpoint of at least one edge — an audited issue with no blocker and no dependent was never drawn by the Deps graph. Idle work dropped too: the automation queue file is encoded only when the queue, its dependency ledger or cron cursors changed (not on every event-loop turn); a Sessions discovery pass that found nothing new no longer stores a snapshot or wakes the dashboards; `tmux -V` runs once per daemon once tmux is found (until then a PATH lookup, so installing tmux is still picked up) and `tmux list-panes` is skipped while no tmux server socket exists; the local tracker filters issue files by state before converting and sorting them, and while its directory watch is healthy rescans every 60 s instead of 10 s (10 s without file events, as before). Gzip for the stream (optional proposal 8) was not added: a gzip stream is per connection, so each client would compress every frame itself (undoing the shared encoding's CPU saving), and sharing compressed bytes would need concatenated gzip members, which browsers' streaming decoders are not guaranteed to handle.

- **Prompt editor: CodeMirror 6 with Markdown and Liquid** (#122). The SOUL, INSTRUCTIONS and automation instruction editors are now a CodeMirror 6 editor instead of a textarea: Markdown highlighting (headings, inline code and fenced blocks, emphasis, links, quotes) and Liquid highlighting for `{{ … }}` objects and `{% … %}` tags, line wrapping, undo history and in-editor search (Ctrl/Cmd+F), coloured from the dashboard's light and dark tokens. The #87 suggestions run on `@codemirror/autocomplete` with the same sources and insertion rules; the list, its keys (arrows, Enter, Escape, plus Ctrl+Space to open it) and its listbox ARIA come from the library, the suggestion count is still announced, Tab still moves focus, and an Escape that closes the list does not close the dialog. Write / Preview and the save flow are unchanged, and saving writes the editor's text as is. The editor is a lazily loaded chunk (about 120 kB gzipped) fetched the first time a prompt field opens; until then the text shows read-only. New dependencies: `@codemirror/{state,view,commands,autocomplete,search,language}`, `@lezer/highlight`, `@lezer/markdown`. See [Agent Profiles](site/src/content/docs/guides/agent-profiles.mdx#the-prompt-editor).

- **The tracker store is on by default** (#132). `tracker.store.enabled` now defaults to `true` for Linear and GitHub: list reads are served from `.itervox/tracker_store.json`, kept current by incremental pulls (#114), and every agent start re-reads its issue by ID first (the claim check, #116), so an issue a person moved out of an active state since the last sync is not dispatched (`TestDefaultStoreDoesNotDispatchAnIssueMovedOutBetweenSyncs` runs the real daemon against a GitHub API whose listings lag behind it). **Upgrade note:** a project with no `tracker.store` block switches from polling to the store on its first start after the upgrade; that start makes one full pull before the first read is answered and writes `.itervox/tracker_store.json` (gitignored by `itervox init`'s `.itervox/.gitignore`). A change made in the tracker reaches the board within `tracker.store.sync_interval_ms` (default 1 minute) rather than at the next tick. To keep polling the tracker directly, set `tracker.store.enabled: false`. `local` and `memory` trackers are unaffected.
- **Headless by default; the terminal UI is deprecated** (#134). `itervox` with no command now runs headless even on a terminal: no terminal UI, logs on stderr, and the dashboard URL printed there (with its token when stderr is a terminal, as before). `itervox --tui` starts the terminal UI, which is deprecated and will be removed in v0.3: its header says so, and the daemon logs a deprecation warning when it starts. Without a terminal, `--tui` warns and runs headless. `--headless` (#120) still withholds the tokenised URL even on a terminal, and wins over `--tui`. **Upgrade note:** if you start Itervox in a terminal and use the terminal UI, add `--tui`; otherwise use the dashboard, or `itervox watch`, `itervox logs -f <issue>` and the quick actions from another shell. This supersedes the #120 entry's "the terminal UI stays the default".

### Removed

- **The terminal UI** (#240). `internal/statusui` (the Bubbletea terminal UI deprecated in v0.2.4, #134), its golden files, `make tui-golden`, the TUI wiring in `cmd/itervox` and the Charm UI dependencies only it used (`bubbletea`, `bubbles`, `x/exp/teatest`, `knz/catwalk`; `charmbracelet/log` and `x/term` stay) are gone. `itervox --tui` now prints one line pointing to `itervox watch` and exits with code 2. With nothing left that puts the terminal into raw mode, `fatalExit` no longer runs `stty sane` (it keeps its runtime-file cleanup) and the daemon's panic paths no longer touch the terminal. After start-up, logs always go to both stderr and the log file.

### Security

- **Go toolchain bumped to 1.26.9 and `golang.org/x/net` to v0.60.0.** `govulncheck` flagged ten standard-library advisories (GO-2026-6603/6605/6607/6608/6609/6610/6611/6612/6613/6617: HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 request handling in `net/http`, `net/textproto` and `crypto/tls`, plus their `x/net` counterparts) whose fixes ship in Go 1.26.9 and 1.27.2 only, so the 1.25 line no longer receives them. `go.mod`, the `Makefile` `GOTOOLCHAIN` pin and the container image's `GO_VERSION` move together; contributors with `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` get the toolchain downloaded on the next build.

### Fixed

- **A slow or rate-limited tracker no longer freezes the daemon** (#187). The poll tick read the tracker inside the event loop with a context that had no deadline, so a Linear outage or a run of 429s could keep one tick in the tracker for minutes: finished workers were not recorded, dashboard actions queued up and then failed, and the snapshot froze. The tick's tracker reads now run off the loop: the running issues' state reconcile, the candidate list and the input-required reply checks are read on a goroutine (one poll in flight at a time) and applied as an event with the state the loop has by then, so a run that ended or was replaced while the poll was in flight is neither stopped nor dispatched again from the poll's older data. The dispatch claim check (#116) reads off the loop too: each pick holds its slot until its read comes back, and nothing starts without it. Every poll runs under a deadline of 3 × `polling.interval_ms` (at least 30 s, at most 2 minutes), so a long rate-limit wait fails fast with the typed rate-limit error instead of blocking; the reads that stay on the loop (due retries, queued input resumes and reviews, automation queue refreshes) share one 30 s deadline per loop iteration. After three polls in a row hit a timeout, network error or 5xx, a tracker circuit breaker skips tracker reads for two poll intervals (30 s to 5 minutes; due retries and queued resumes wait without spending an attempt) and then probes the tracker. A poll running past the interval plus half an interval is logged at warn, and the poll's state (running for Xs, slow, degraded) shows on the snapshot (`trackerPoll`), a dashboard tile, `HEARTBEAT.md` (`- Poll:`) and `/api/v1/ready` (degraded). `/api/v1/ready`'s tick budget drops from 10 minutes to 2 minutes, and model discovery (`itervox models refresh` and the dashboard's model refresh) uses an HTTP client with a 15 s timeout instead of `http.DefaultClient`.
- **The shared bare clone keeps fetching while worktrees have branches checked out** (#195). With `workspace.worktree: true` and a `clone_url`, the clone under `<workspace.root>/.bare` fetched with `+refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*`, mapping origin's branches onto its local branches. git refuses to update a branch a worktree has checked out, so as soon as any worktree held a branch that also exists on origin (almost always) every `git fetch --all --prune` exited 128 (`refusing to fetch into branch ... checked out at ...`); the failure was only a WARN line, so `main` and every `base_branch` silently stopped moving and new worktrees started from old code. The same mapping made local branches look like remote-tracking ones, which is how a new worktree branch came to track the branch it was made from (#193's root cause), and its forced `+` update would have reset a branch no worktree held to origin's version, dropping unpushed commits. Now: the clone fetches into `refs/remotes/origin/*` (`+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`) and a fetch never writes a local branch; new worktrees start from `origin/<base_branch>`; `git worktree add` runs with `--no-track`, and a new branch's only upstream is its own name on origin when origin has it (otherwise none until the agent's `git push -u origin HEAD`); a branch only origin has (an open PR's, or one pushed before its worktree was cleared) is created from `origin/<branch>`, and an existing local copy is fast-forwarded to it — never rewound, and never while a worktree has it checked out (#193's branch-in-use hold still applies); the clone's local base branch (HEAD's branch) is fast-forwarded the same way after each fetch so HEAD, stacking and restack keep a current base. A failing fetch is recorded once per distinct error in recent failures (kind `workspace_fetch`) until a fetch succeeds, and `itervox doctor` reports the clone's last successful fetch, a failing fetch (`ERROR`, exit 1), a fetch older than 24 h (`WARNING`) and a clone still on the old refspec (`WARNING`). Directory mode (`worktree: false`) and worktree mode without `clone_url` are unaffected: each uses a clone with the standard `refs/remotes/origin/*` refspec. Documented in [configuration](docs/configuration.md#workspace).
- **Issues no longer take over another issue's pull request branch, and a branch checked out elsewhere is held instead of retried** (#193). Root cause: in the shared bare clone the fetch refspec maps origin's branches onto `refs/heads/*`, so git set every new worktree branch to track the branch it was made from; a dependent stacked on its blocker's branch therefore tracked the blocker's branch, the post-run `gh pr view` (no argument, so resolved through that upstream) returned the blocker's open PR, the worker commented it on the dependent as "Pull request created", and the dependent's next dispatch read that URL back as its own PR and tried `git worktree add` on the blocker's branch — which git refuses while the blocker's worktree has it, failing identically on every retry (53 failures across 8 issues in the report). Now: the post-run lookup passes the worktree's branch to `gh pr view` explicitly; the open-PR lookup continues a linked PR only when it is the issue's own (head branch is the issue's branch or names the identifier as a whole token, or the title/body names the identifier on word boundaries or links the tracker issue); before `git worktree add` the workspace reads `git worktree list --porcelain` and reports a branch checked out in another live worktree as a typed `BranchInUseError` (git's "is already used by worktree at" and older "is already checked out at" refusals are typed the same way), while a stale registration of the issue's own worktree is pruned and re-created; the orchestrator holds such an issue with the new `branch_in_use` ineligible reason (event-loop state, shown in `/api/v1/issues` and the dashboard as "Branch checked out elsewhere", recorded once in recent failures) instead of scheduling a retry, and releases it on the first tick after the other worktree frees the branch. Fetches (and the first clone) into one shared repository are serialized per repository on the worker goroutines, so parallel dispatches no longer fail with `cannot lock ref`. Documented in [configuration](docs/configuration.md#workspace).
- **Cron automations with `filter.limit` rotate through every matching issue** (#176). A `cron` rule with more matching issues than its `limit` used to pick the same first N (in identifier order) every tick, so the rest were never reached. Each rule now keeps a cursor, the last issue it served: the next tick starts after it, wraps around, and serves at most `limit` issues, so 7 matches with `limit: 3` are all served within three ticks and none twice before every one has been served once. An issue that already has a run or a queued dispatch from the rule is skipped without using a slot, and an issue that left the filter drops out of the rotation. The selection now happens in the orchestrator's event loop (the scheduler hands it every match in one `DispatchCronBatch` event) and the cursor is event-loop state, saved as `cron_cursors` in `automation_queue.json`, so a restart resumes the rotation. Cron rules without `limit` and the event-polled triggers behave as before. Guide: [`limit`](site/src/content/docs/guides/automations.mdx#limit).
- **An agent moving its own issue no longer stops its worker mid-finish** (#177). When an agent opened its PR and then moved its issue out of the active states (the `move_state` action, typically to `tracker.completion_state`) before its turn ended, the move landed in the tracker at once and the next reconciliation tick stopped the worker as if a person had closed the issue: its post-PR tracker comment, its handoff file and the `pr_opened` dispatch were lost (2 of 11 issues in the #173 pilot). A `move_state` on an issue whose worker is still running, to a state that would stop that worker, is now deferred until the worker exits: the worker ends its turn loop as it would after a landed move and finishes normally, then the move is applied, only while the tracker still shows the state the agent moved the issue from. When the worker applied `completion_state` itself on a successful run, that move stands and the deferred one is dropped, as when the agent's move landed first. Until the move is applied the issue is not dispatched or retried (`state_move_pending`). Deferred moves persist to `deferred_state_moves.json` in the daemon log directory, so a restart while the worker runs does not lose them; the next daemon applies them on its first tick. A person moving the issue (dashboard or tracker) is never deferred and still stops the worker; a move the agent had deferred is then dropped. Guide: [Moving the issue while its worker is still running](site/src/content/docs/guides/automations.mdx#moving-the-issue-while-its-worker-is-still-running). Also fixed: the `pr_opened` dispatch a successful run sends right after its exit was bound to the worker's context, which the event loop cancels while handling that exit, so whenever the loop handled the exit first the dispatch was silently dropped; it is now sent detached from that context (still bounded by its timeout and by the loop's exit), and a skipped send is logged.

- **The automation event poll no longer exhausts the tracker's rate limit on large projects** (#155). The poll behind `tracker_comment_added`, `issue_entered_state` and `issue_moved_to_backlog` listed every backlog, active and terminal issue, with relations, every 15 seconds: on a 1,600-issue Linear project the daemon was rate-limited within twenty minutes of starting, and the terminal states alone cost about 1,440 of Linear's 2,500 requests an hour. It now fetches only the states its rules need: each rule's `filter.states` and `trigger.state`, the active states, and the backlog states only when an `issue_moved_to_backlog` rule exists; terminal states and `completion_state` only when a rule names them. With no such rule it makes no request at all. A move into a polled state from one the poll no longer fetches (Backlog → Todo, Done → Backlog) still fires, with an empty `{{ trigger.previous_state }}`; an issue created in the trigger state still does not, and neither does one that only became visible because the dashboard's project filter was widened. A `tracker_comment_added` rule without `filter.states` now watches comments on active issues only (terminal issues were never dispatched by any automation); name other states in `filter.states` to watch them. New setting `polling.automation_interval_ms` (default 15000) sets the poll's interval, separate from the 15-second cron check; while the tracker reports less than 20% of its request budget left, the interval doubles after each poll up to 8× and returns once the budget recovers. With the tracker store on (the default), the poll's state set becomes a store view after one fetch and is kept current by the store's incremental "updated since" pull (#114), so repeated polls make no list request.

- **Reviewers are identified by their own run, and a review no longer clears your profile choice** (#127). A reviewer's retry, a reviewer re-dispatched after its backend was limited, a paused reviewer and a reviewer waiting for input (across a restart too) now run as the same reviewer under its own profile. Reviewer runs no longer set the issue's profile: a profile you picked for an issue stays in place through its review instead of being replaced while the reviewer ran and deleted when it finished, and picking a profile while a reviewer retry is pending no longer turns that retry into an implementer run. The review chain advances from the finishing reviewer's own run record, so a reviewer stopped by reconcile still counts once, never twice. A reviewer whose vendor-limit re-dispatch is held (every mapped backend limited) continues as a reviewer retry that keeps the claim, so the next poll cannot start it as implementer work. A review chain is kept while its reviewer waits for input, has a reply queued, is paused or is pending during a drain, even with the issue outside the active states, so the resumed reviewer still advances it.

- **Every run has an ID and a lifecycle** (#125). Each dispatch gets a run ID (also its log session ID), carried on every update and exit its worker sends, and a phase: dispatched, running, finishing, exited. The exit or progress of a run that was stopped and replaced by a new run on the same issue is recognised by its ID and no longer touches the new run, even after the new run has itself exited and left a retry; before, a late exit deleted the new run, cancelled its worker and could schedule a retry or a review for it. A run that is finishing (its worker has moved the issue to `completion_state`, or is sending its exit) is left to its own exit by tracker reconciliation and by stall detection.

- **An issue with an empty description no longer fails its prompt** (#102). `{{ issue.description }}`, `{{ issue.url }}` and `{{ issue.branch_name }}` print as nothing when empty, instead of failing the dispatch with `undefined variable` under strict variables; `{% if issue.description %}` still skips its block, and a misspelt variable such as `{{ issue.descripton }}` still fails. The Linear guide's example prompt, which printed the description unguarded, now works on issues without one.

- **Itervox runs on its own repository** (#78). The repo's `WORKFLOW.md` is migrated to schema 2 (comments kept). `before_run` only fetches, and fast-forwards `main` when the workspace is still on it, so a resumed or retried run keeps its branch and unpushed work. The prompt checks out an existing issue branch (local or pushed) before creating one, and runs `make verify` instead of `go test ./...`. The `go-toolchain-sync` skill's description is quoted so strict YAML (and the skills inventory) can read it.

- **Reviewer runs are no longer stopped on an in-review issue** (found while doing #79). A reviewer is dispatched on an issue the implementer just moved to `tracker.completion_state`, usually a state that is neither active nor terminal (`in-review`), and reconciliation stopped any run on such an issue, so a review could be cut off before it finished. Reviewer runs now keep running while the issue is in `completion_state`; any other non-active state (an operator moving it to backlog) or a terminal state still stops them.
- **Saving a profile from the dashboard no longer strips `permission_mode`** (found while doing #80). The dashboard does not edit it, and the save rebuilt the profile without it, so a profile set to `sandbox` silently went back to `bypass` in `WORKFLOW.md`. It (and the new `require_evidence`) is now carried over from the saved profile.
- **Restacking now really skips a running dependent** (found while doing #73). The safety check looked the issue up by identifier in `state.Running`, which is keyed by issue ID, so it never matched: a running dependent could be rebased under its agent, with only the uncommitted-changes check in the way. It now matches by ID and by identifier, and the skipped restack (and the pull request retarget) runs on the first dependency audit that finds the dependent idle; before, the unblock was consumed and the restack never happened.
- **The GitHub tracker no longer re-posts the branch marker comment on retries** (#72). GitHub records an issue's working branch as a hidden `<!-- itervox:branch:… -->` comment. A worker posts it whenever it does not already know the branch, and a retry whose first-turn issue-detail fetch failed starts from the list-fetched issue, which never carries one, so each such retry posted an identical comment and notified the issue's watchers again. `SetIssueBranch` now reads the latest marker first and posts only when it names a different branch; if the comments cannot be read it still posts, so the branch is never lost. Linear, which stores the branch in a field, is unchanged.
- **The GitHub tracker no longer treats pull requests as issues** (#70). GitHub's `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues` lists pull requests as well, and the tracker never filtered them, so an open pull request carrying an active-state label (`todo`, `in-progress`) became a dispatch candidate, and the `closed` fetch pulled every closed or merged pull request into the terminal-state lists. Items with a non-null `pull_request` object are now skipped in the shared paginated fetch, which covers candidates, `closed`, and label-state fetches such as the backlog.
- **`itervox init --update` no longer drops comments or reorders `WORKFLOW.md` keys** (#71). The schema-2 migration decoded the front matter into a map and re-marshalled it, which deleted every comment (including the GitHub tracker label setup notes) and sorted all keys alphabetically, with `itervox_schema_version: 2` landing in the middle of the file. The migration now edits the YAML node tree: comments, key order, quoting, block scalars, flow sequences, blank lines between sections and the file's indent width are preserved, the schema marker is inserted as the first key, and only the migrated keys change. `WORKFLOW.md.bak` behaviour is unchanged. A profile written as an alias of an anchored mapping (`name: *defaults`) or merging one (`<<: *defaults`) is migrated to the same effective profile, with an inherited `prompt:` moved out like an own one; the anchor itself is left as written. Before replacing the workflow, the migration checks that every migrated profile reads back as intended, and leaves the file unchanged otherwise.
- **Removed a stale startup warning that claimed multi-reviewer fan-out was disabled** (#69). Fan-out has run every `agent.reviewer_profiles` entry since 0.2.1 (#58), but config loading still logged `multi-reviewer fan-out is disabled in this release; only the first agent.reviewer_profiles entry runs` whenever more than one reviewer was listed, so operators were told the opposite of what the daemon did. The warning and its stale rationale are gone; a `reviewer_profiles`-only config still promotes its first entry into `reviewer_profile` (now logged at INFO, since that configuration is valid). The 0.2.1 notes carried a contradictory "fan-out is disabled" bullet alongside the one announcing it runs; the wrong bullet is removed.
- **GCP provisioning stopped before Cloud NAT existed** (#154). `deploy/gcp/provision.sh` (without `--public`) passed `--auto-allocate-nat-external-ip`, which `gcloud compute routers nats create` rejects as an unrecognized argument (the flag is plural, `--auto-allocate-nat-external-ips`). The VM, its data disk, the IAP firewall rule and the router were created, but no NAT, so the VM had no egress and `bootstrap.sh` could not download anything. The flag is fixed, and `deploy/gcp/provision_test.sh` (run by `make deploy-test`) drives the script against a `gcloud` stub that refuses any flag the real command does not accept.
